claims.statement: The Met describes Scythian migration to the northern Black Sea region in the late eighth century BCE and substantial replacement by Sarmatian groups by the late second century BCE.
Politically diverse pastoral horse-riding communities traded and interacted with neighbouring Greek settlements.

evidence.note: 750–100 BCE is a rounded editorial envelope for the source’s late-century boundaries. It is not a precise migration date or the end of all Scythian communities. A mobile, diverse population is not represented by one point or a single state border.
